posts.name: Praion
posts.cooked:
As someone who only has the App (for now) I was really excited for OX and CR but now I find not wanting to play them much. 

 

I thought I would really like OX because the theme is super cool while CR didn't appeal to me, just a blaster with some ongoings, I thought. 

 

CR I like playing more now. However, the gameplay is super repetitive. Becasue of the ammount of Cantrips and Tutors you do a lot of the same stuff every game. Get By Any Means, Get the Hat, Get the Bow or Danny Boy and then just attack until they are dead, playing extra bounties when you get them. 
Every game is very much the same. It's powerful when getting going but the gameplay is repetitive. Are you also feeling this? 

 

OX however feels different enough and there is some tricky stuff you can do but it never really feels like I am doing much. I think this is because OX does a lot of stuff at the beginning of turn. A normal hero who is fully set up does most stuff at the end of turn. There they explode. OX does a lot of stuff at the beginning but that feels more like bookkeeping then like doing something big and explosive. When you get a good plating blast (?) off that is cool at the end of turn but otherwise you are just kinda playing another card. 
Is there something I am missing there? How can I get more enjoyment out of OX?

posts.name: Ameena
posts.cooked:
Jim is among my favourite heroes :D. He's really good at focusing down single targets, and somewhat less good at most other things. He can help a little with a few other bits and pieces, such as using The Whole Gang to insta-kill a low-hp target or a Temporal Grenade to take out an environment card or something. I don't know what you mean by "cantrips and tutors" but based on the context I'm guessing you're referring to his ability to search for stuff fairly easily? I find Jim is fun to play when I want to just wreck something...him versus Plague Rat is good, you can do about twenty damage in a single turn with just your own deck and a little help from the Rat himself (get Infected ASAP and don't bother taking out the Locus >:)). I suppose it is kind of repetitive but I've not got bored with him yet...though I don't think I've ever played one hero twice in a row except for rare occasions when all the heroes get wiped within the first couple of rounds meaning I've been taken out before I had a chance to really do anything. It's good that Jim has means of dealing damage even if the bad guys have soak - it just adds an extra layer of challenge, really. Bad guy got soak? Get out the Masadah and any Bounty (the more the better, obviously) and you can at least hurt it with your Power phase (plus the bonus Power use if Ultimate Target is out and that target hits something) :).

With Omni-10, the fact he does most of his stuff at the start of his turn is kind of his thing, really. I like the fun of getting all eight components out, then having them all go off and then going "...and now it's my Play phase" and doing even more stuff :D. On more than one occasion I have used Singularity as a finishing move by blowing up everyone's equipment and dealing 20+ damage (assuming the other heroes have a few equipment cards each) :D. I think with Omni-10 once I'm set up I kind of see the Start phase as the main bit of his turn and the rest as a bunch of bonus actions that I happen to be able to do (even though with every other hero the only time they tend to get to do anything in their Start phases is when one of their ongoigns runs out or they skip their turn to take out an environment card or something). He has a bunch of nice cards - Disruptive Flechettes is nice in a high-target environment, for example, regardless of whether or not there are any hostile ongoings you want to deal with. Defensive Blast can get ridiculous if you can get a few damage buffs. Ablative Coating and an RPS against Plague Rat is fun, too - Plague Rat hits you for irreducible toxic damage, you hit him back. You get Infected and hit yourself for irreducible toxic damage, you then hit Plague Rat and heal yourself off your Innervation Rays :D. Omni-10 is also amazing at getting around any "You cannot do X" things, such as half the cards in Megalopolis, as nothing ever stops you doing stuff in your Start phase...and evne if you use said phase to skip it to get rid of an environment card that requires that you do so, you still don't get to the "skip your turn" part until you've used any components that were in play before the thing that requires you to skip your turn. So you still might be able to do a bunch of stuff if you had all of them out and then the Volcanic Eruption showed up ;).

But all that aside, what you find enjoyable is going to differ from what at least a few other people find enjoyable - it may be that neither of these heroes are the ones for you and that you will just always have more fun with certain other ones. I enjoy playing both of the Shattered Timelines heroes - as mentioned at the start of this post, Jim is one of my favourites because it is fun to just pound away at something with self-buffed damage and wreck it :D. But my other top wo heroes are the Adept and probably the Naturalist, both of whom are pretty versatile and the former is my top-top favourite just because I can do sooo muuuuch thiiiinnnngs :D. And I hardly ever deal damage with him, so it's not like I only play heroes to set up and nuke stuff (or take it out a chunk at a time, as Jim does). I think I just like versatility, to be able to still do something even when some other action is blocked.

posts.name: VikenXetred
posts.cooked:
Me and my buddy played a game last week vs Baron Blade using Legacy, Omnitron X, and Parse. While Parse did nothing in the end, Baron Blade got wrecked by OX and OX alone essentially, with a little outside help from Legacy. First turn, Legacy got Inspiring Presence out, and from then on he used his hero power each round, occasionally using cards to deal a little damage or draw. With that, Omnitron was dealing +2 damage per card. 

After BB played Backlash Field, OX got Elemental Exochassis out, reducing damage he recieved by 2, then played Reactive Plating Subroutine. This made so whenever BB dealt OX any Energy damage, OX was hitting back for 4 Energy damage, causing BB to hit back with Backlash Field for 3-2=1, and again OX would hit back for 4 lightning damage.

OX got even more powerful after playing Defensive Blast. Would discard a plating card, and deal 3 damage to each enemy for each damage type on the card. Add all that up with a couple of components to improve his play a bit more (Electro-Deployment Unit to draw more cards and Innervation ray to stay healed), and he tanked and slaughtered BB.

I realize BB is a level 1 boss, but OX was easily clocking out 20 damage a round by the end, and BB is a relatively short fight. I think we had maybe 6-8 rounds before the game ended. (thanks to OX's inate power)

 

In short, the fun part of OX is combining his ongoings and equipment together, and working with other heroes. He can keep his damage spread out fairly easily, even more so if you are lucky enough to get his 2 lasting limited cards out. I find him best played with heroes that make him stronger or against villains that have a lot of targets.

posts.name: Foote
posts.cooked:
There might be a disconnect between the physical game and the digital game.

When OX gets going and you have all those equipment cards in play on the table and playing/drawing cards, dealing irreducible damage, healing, it feels like you are building a big arsenal on your little robot. To me, seeing your massive buildup is pretty satisfying, and when all of that gets destroyed from damage the "oh shit" moment is that much bigger. Getting off really big Defensive Blasts are very satisfying as well and playing Fletches feels so good after years of being on the opposite end of those fletches from the base game.

But ultimately if you don't find the same thing satisfying im not sure anyone can talk you into liking it. I havn't played him on digital so Im not sure how the feeling changes, but I love playing OX on the table.

Chrono you just have to realize that most of the "damage only" type characters lack a ton of nuiance because they have one primary purpose. Chrono, Ra, KNYFE, Expat, they all can feel repetitive beacuse your goal with those decks is fairly limited to "do as much damage as possible" and they all have their way of doing exactly that. What I like about Chrono compared to the others in that list is his out of turn power uses and the way his damage favors multipliers and team support to really shine, which in turn highlights the cooperative component of the game. Watching his bow go from 1+1 to 5+5 and just wailing on his bounty targets has a nice thematic feel for me and it satisfies my itch for that kind of gameplay.

Thats just my experience with them.

posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
Chrono Ranger, for me, his big blow-out turns are about Hunter and Hunted once you've got several Bounties out -- combine it with The Ultimate Target against someone like Akash'Bhuta, The Matriarch or The Operative who's going to do a lot of out-of-turn damage. I've had CR knock dozens of HP off targets in a single turn, wipe out minions with Danny Boy or just keep the villain's damage so low it's inconsequential.

You haven't seen what he can do until you've popped off Hunter and Hunted, followed by a Terrible Tech Strike and the Compounded Bow all in one round -- it's just plain devastating.

He's also, as far as I know, the only hero who can search his deck for Environment/Ongoing destruction.

Part of the issue, I think, is they're both, in a way, utility based. A lot of CR's bounties are great, but situational, while OX does a lot of plinking with no inherent way to boost his damage. He's very much a finesse character.

OX is one of my favorites to play around with because he can do everything. While it's true that you'll end up with rounds where you don't play much (I almost never use Self Sabotage or Singularity, and always seem to end up a couple copies of each in hand), his power is always useful (any set-up heavy hero loves it, Unity especially), and he can singlehandedly keep the Environment in check and smack the villain around at the same time. He's also very reliable when it comes to irreducible damage -- between the Focused Plasma Blaster and his plating cards, he can practically take out Voss single-handedly, and he's The Organization's worse nightmare, especially in a 3-hero game.

OX is really a team-player, nearly as much as AA. If you find yourself with little to do, look to Timeshift your pals, especially if you have someone who can let you peek at or stack the decks.

One fun team I had started with Scholar and then OX. Scholar soakes up all the damage, then OX heals him twice every round so he can blast stuff.

posts.name: riff.freelance
posts.cooked:
It's a perspective thing I think. 
 
Omni X is a high setup character IMHO. If you get him set up it feels very satisfying. It is also very nice to support your team or be supported by them. That's kinda unique to Omni X. You can be the buffed damage dealer, or give card plays to make someone else that guy. You can tank, you can heal. Omni is almost a Swiss Army knife.  That's my two cents on our robot pal. Oh special note: Omni X and Unity work real well together, between that and the ARG I have started to almost ship them. 
 
 
 
Chrono Ranger is a damage dealer. They are a bit more linear in gameplay. If this isn't your playstyle that might be a reason you don't like him. For me it's getting going and doing 7+ damage every turn (easy enough with some work) and enjoying it. Sweeping minions and still plinking the boss is nice. Taking big chunks out of a target is fun. Last night I had fun playing Sudden Contract to play the kill me and draw bounty then killing said target only to follow up with Bounty Board giving me back the bounty card. It's coming up with clever interactions between the tutor cards and the steady stream of damage that make CR fun. 
 
Hope my opinions help. Cheers!!!

posts.cooked:
Start of turn is your turn as OX.

That's what you are building up, that's where the value is.

Once you get your components going you slow down and Timeshift other decks, you want to save your resets for component wipes and make the team awesome with your power.  Don't sweat drawing a lot with your start of turn stuff if your components are rolling, you are doing awesome, and at that point you focus on your allies decks and save up advancement's and Reset's for when you have to rebuild.

 

People love Chrono because you get really great build up with him.

I'm not a big fan myself.

I think I have been using Reset wrong a lot. Using it to just cycle and draw a card is not really worth much. It hsould be used to get a chance to draw all my played components again. It seems minor but reset should be used with a purpose I suppose. Must try this next time I play. 

 

It's perfectly fine to cycle Reset, especially if you don't have great options in your hand.  The time I hold it are when I have a decent number of components (3 or more) and either no plating/the wrong plating/facingtargets who do a bunch of different types of damage
